**D-1: How should a stored number with no country code (e.g. `020 7946 0000`) be normalised?**
- **a) Only international numbers.** Only numbers written with `+` or `00` are normalised. Every national-format number gets an empty `phone_e164`. It never guesses, but fewer customers get a number, and the plan reports how many.
- **b) One default country** that you name (e.g. `D-1=b` plus the country). More customers get a number, but a customer from another country who typed a national number gets a wrong number that can still be dialled.

**D-2: How should users store `phone_e164` and fill it for existing customers?**
- **a) New column plus a one-off backfill command.** Migration 002 adds a nullable column (with an undo). Each update writes it. The backfill runs in batches, can be rerun, and reports how many it filled and left empty.
- **b) Fill it when a customer is read or written.** Customers who are never read stay empty, and reads start writing to the database.
- **c) No column; compute it on every read.** This doesn't store the number as PRD-3.1 asks, and every read pays the cost.
- Recommended **a**: it is the only option that stores and fills every customer while reads stay read-only. Default: **a**, not safe to apply without you.

- **a) Add `github.com/nyaruka/phonenumbers`.** It is the Go version of Google's libphonenumber and checks country codes and lengths per country. It is one new dependency whose rules change several times a year.
- **b) Standard library only.** It strips separators and checks for 8–15 digits. Numbers with a wrong country code or length still pass, so some stored numbers won't be dialable.

CHG-001 now has its specs and is waiting for your decisions. The risk is **CRITICAL**. It moved through draft → investigating → specified → awaiting_decisions, and the spec step ended OK.

**Why it's CRITICAL:** removing `name` from `GET /v1/users/{id}` breaks a service outside this change. That service is notifications, which reads this endpoint in prod at about 6 req/min. Nobody has checked whether it uses `name`, and nobody knows who owns it. Two more things raise the risk:
- Two services change: users (owned by `@acme/identity`) and Orders (owned by `@acme/commerce`).
- There is no traffic data for the clients of Orders' `/v1/orders/{id}/customer`. That endpoint passes the users response through unchanged, so the rename reaches them too.

The customer's name is personal data, so the plan must include a security review task. Orders needs no code change, only a contract test that `display_name` passes through and `name` is not added.

## Decisions

**D-1: What about notifications, which may read `name`?**
- **a) Hold the users release for a check.** The first task finds the notifications owner and gets their sign-off that it doesn't read `name`. This is the safest option, but the release date depends on another team.
- **b) Ship and tell the owner in the PR.** This is the fastest option. If notifications reads `name`, its messages lose the customer's name from the release on.
- **c) Add notifications to this change.** It would read `display_name` and release together with users. This needs its repo and its owner's approval, and adds a third service.
- Recommended and default: **a**. The cutover can't fall back to `name`, and a check costs only one task.

**D-2: Should the database column `users.name` be renamed too?**
- **a) Change the API field only and keep the column.** There is no migration, and rollback is a redeploy.
- **b) Rename the column as well.** This adds a migration on a live table whose size is unknown. Anything else that reads the column breaks, and rollback needs the reverse migration.
- Recommended and default: **a**. The PRD only asks for the API rename.

**D-3: What should a `PUT` that still sends `name` get back?**
- **a) A 400 error, with a message pointing to `display_name`.** Other unknown fields keep today's behaviour.
- **b) A 200, with `name` silently dropped.** An out-of-date client would quietly stop updating the customer's name.
- Recommended and default: **a**. The client fails loudly and knows what to change.

**D-4: Open PR acme/users#812 (SHOP-12, phone formats) edits the same `api/user.go`. How should this change work alongside it?**
- **a) Build from main.** The PR body asks the #812 author to rebase on whichever of the two merges second. There will be one small conflict in the struct.
- **b) Build on top of #812.** There's no conflict, but this change can only merge after #812, so the release date follows SHOP-12.

# CHG-001 needs four decisions before planning

CHG-001 renames the customer field `name` to `display_name` in GET/PUT /v1/users/{id}. The investigation and the specs are done, and the change is now `awaiting_decisions`.

**Risk level: CRITICAL.** The rename changes three endpoints in a way that breaks their callers: GET and PUT `/v1/users/{id}`, and GET `/v1/orders/{id}/customer`. That last one belongs to orders, which copies the users reply into its own response unchanged, so its callers see the rename too. No one has identified the callers of these endpoints, and Prometheus has no per-client traffic to find them with. The change also touches personal data, and no security review is planned yet.

**Not affected:**
- **Notifications and the `users.updated.v1` event:** the event sends only `id` and `phone`.
- **The `users.name` database column:** only the JSON field is renamed, so there is no migration.
- **The gateway:** it routes requests without reading them.

**Specs:**
- **users:** GET and PUT use `display_name`, and a PUT that still sends `name` is rejected if you answer D-1=a.
- **orders:** no code change, only a test that the customer endpoint now returns `display_name`.

## Cards

**D-2: The callers are unknown. How should the rename proceed without a transition period?**
The PRD says every client already uses `display_name`, but nothing verifies that.
- **a: Verify callers before release.** The plan starts by listing callers from 7 days or more of access logs, and each client owner, including @acme/commerce for orders, confirms the switch. The release waits for those confirmations. This is slower, but no client is surprised.
- **b: Trust the PRD and release.** You announce the change to client teams and roll back by redeploying the previous image. This is fastest, but any unknown caller breaks in production until the rollback.
- **c: Release with a breakage watch.** Same as b, plus users logs each request that still sends `name`, and the 4xx rate is watched against a rollback threshold. You see breakage within minutes, but users hit it first.
- **Recommended:** a. The only evidence that clients have switched is the PRD's statement. **Default:** a (safe).

**D-1: What should happen to a PUT that still sends `name`?**
Today unknown keys in the body are silently ignored, so an old client's name edit would be lost without any error.
- **a: Reject with 400.** The error message tells the caller to send `display_name`. Old clients fail loudly and nothing is lost silently.
- **b: Ignore the field.** The request succeeds, but the name edit is lost with no signal to anyone.
- **Recommended:** a, the only way an old client notices. **Default:** a. This default is **not marked safe**, because it breaks old clients visibly.

**D-4: In which order should this change and the open PR acme/users#812 (SHOP-12) land?**
PR #812 ("Normalise phone formats") edits the same file, `users/api/user.go`.
- **a: Build on main, and whichever PR merges second rebases.** No waiting, one conflict to resolve later.
- **b: Build on top of #812's branch.** No conflict, but this change ships only after #812 and inherits any rework it needs.
- **c: Wait until #812 merges, then build on main.** No conflict, but the rename waits for #812's review.
- **Recommended:** a. The overlap is one struct and one handler. **Default:** a (safe).

No security report yet.

## Side findings (not fixed here)

- SF-4 (security, high) api/user.go:25-28: CWE-862 / CWE-639. Register mounts GET and PUT /v1/users/{id} with no authentication or authorization, and putUser takes the user id from the path and announces a phone change for it (events.PublishUserUpdated, which per its comment writes users.users.phone). Any caller that reaches the service can read any profile and overwrite any user's phone, a field this service owns and every other service reads. main.go:13-15 also starts the server with http.ListenAndServe and no read, header or idle timeouts (the gosec warning is suppressed as a fixture server). Pre-existing, not introduced by T-02. → not decided yet
- SF-5 (security, high) api/customer.go:12-31: CWE-862 / CWE-639. Register mounts GET /v1/orders/{id}/customer with no authentication or authorization, and customer derives the customer id from the client-supplied order id (customerOf) and relays the full users body, which per clients/users.go:9 includes the customer's phone number. Any caller that reaches orders can enumerate order ids and read every customer's profile and phone. Pre-existing, not introduced by T-03 (test-only); the orders side of SF-4. → not decided yet
- SF-6 (security, medium) api/customer.go:20-20: CWE-918 / CWE-20. r.PathValue("id") is the unescaped path segment, so a request to /v1/orders/x%2F..%2F..%2F..%2Fanything/customer yields id "x/../../../anything", and clients/users.go:11 concatenates it unescaped into Base + "/v1/users/c-" + id. - SF-8 (security, low) api/customer.go:21-23: CWE-209. When the users call fails, customer writes the "users unreachable" prefix followed by err.Error() to the client; Go's url.Error text includes the full upstream URL (internal users base address and path), so internal topology is disclosed to any caller. Pre-existing, not introduced by T-03; TestUsersUnreachable asserts only the prefix. → not decided yet
- SF-1 (bug, high) users/api/user.go:24-26: getUser answers with User{ID: r.PathValue(id)} and never reads the stored profile, so GET /v1/users/id always returns an empty name and an empty phone. orders relays this body to its clients and its users client comment says it reads the phone for order notifications (orders/clients/users.go:9), so those reads get no phone. → not decided yet
- SF-2 (bug, medium) orders/clients/users.go:14-17: Users.LegacyProfile calls GET /v1/users/id/legacy-profile and its comment says the receipt job still calls it, but users removed the legacy profile endpoint in 2026-09 (users/api/user.go:1) and users registers only GET and PUT /v1/users/id, so every receipt job call gets 404. → not decided yet
- SF-7 (reliability, medium) clients/users.go:10-17: CWE-400. Users.Get and LegacyProfile call http.Get on the default client, which has no timeout and no request context, so a slow or hung users service holds an orders handler goroutine and connection indefinitely; customer (api/customer.go:31) also io.Copies the users body with no size limit. Pre-existing, not introduced by T-03. → not decided yet
- SF-3 (reliability, low) events/retry.go:3-10: PublishWithRetry calls send in a tight loop with no backoff, attempt limit or context, so a persistently failing send spins a CPU forever. It has no callers in the repo today. → not decided yet
